To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AMPK and CAM kinase are involved in the regulation of muscle mitochondrial biogenesis and glucose uptake in L6 myocytes and in muscle.

AMP kinase and Ca2+/cal-modulin-dependent protein kinase are the two main signaling mechanisms that regulate the expression of proteins involved in the adaptation of muscle mitochondria and the glucose transport system.

the decrease in levels of ATP and increase in Ca2+ that occur during exercise initiate a cascade of events that leads to the increased expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis and increased levels of GLUT4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of calcium and AMPK in the regulation of GLUT4 and mitochondrial enzymes.
the mechanisms responsible for the adaptive changes in muscle mitochondria that occur during endurance training.
understanding the mechanisms by which contractile activity increases the levels of mitochondrial proteins and GLUT4 in muscle and the role of calcium and AMPK in these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AMPK-Ca2+-PGC-1 pathway is a major pathway for the regulation of mitochondrial and glucose transport capacity in skeletal muscle.
AMPK and Ca2+ are important signals in the adaptation to contractile activity and that the increase in the concentration of PGC- 1 is a key event in the initiation of these adaptations.

exercise induces the activation of AMPK and Ca2+/cal-modulin-dependent kinase, which activate PGC1, which in turn binds to various transcriptional factors, leading to the coordinated regulation of gene expression that results in increased levels of mitochondrial enzymes, mitochondrial proteins and GLUT4 in muscle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increase in mitochondrial biogenesis and glucose transport capacity in skeletal muscle during exercise is mediated by the decrease in high-energy phosphates that activate AMP kinase and the increase in Ca2+ that activates CAMK.
exercise increases cytosolic Ca and activates CAMK.
exercise increases cytoplasmic calcium and AMP, which activate Ca2+/cal-modulin kinase (CAMK) and AMP kinase (AMPk), respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increase in cytoplasmic free Ca2+ and activation of AMP kinase by exercise or other stimuli are the signals that initiate the adaptive responses in mitochondria and glucose uptake in muscle.
both the AMPK and CAM pathways are involved in the regulation of the mitochondrial biogenesis and expression of GLUT4.
AMP kinase and CAMK are important regulators of mitochondrial biogenesis in muscle.
